problem: PointGoal navigation agents that are near-perfect (99.6% SR) with noiseless sensing, noiseless actuation and GPS+Compass collapse to 0.3% success under realistic noisy RGB-D, noisy actuation and no localization sensor. Prior SOTA (particle SLAM-net) reaches only 64.5% SR and is slow.
motivation: Real robots have neither perfect GPS+Compass indoors nor noise-free perception and actuation, so localization must come from egocentric observations. Retraining RL policies costs billions of frames, so a separately trained, cheap visual odometry (VO) module that replaces GPS+Compass could reuse existing policies.
key_idea: Train a robust noise-aware VO model offline (geometric invariance losses, dropout pseudo-ensemble, depth discretization, top-down soft projection, per-action models) and use it as a drop-in replacement for GPS+Compass in a pretrained DD-PPO policy.
insight: Each robustness ingredient adds accuracy, and the ablations show gains are not simply from more parameters or data augmentation. Separate per-action models (SepAct) raise SR from 68 to 75, while a 3x wider unified model drops to 70. The geometric invariance losses help, but plain data augmentation does not. RGB-D beats depth-only VO, contrary to prior belief. Dropout with one scaled forward pass beats 10 sampled passes (68 vs 42 SR) and runs at 118.8 vs 8.45 FPS.
method: VO model: ResNet-18 over the stacked pair of processed observations ψ(I_t), ψ(I_t+1) (RGB, depth, discretized depth, soft top-down projection), followed by 2 FC layers that regress SE(2) motion (ξx, ξz, θ). The estimate is integrated into the goal position via v_{t+1}=H·v_t.

Geometric invariance losses: rotation loss (θ_{t→t+1}+θ_{t+1→t})² and translation loss ||ξ_{t→t+1}+R·ξ_{t+1→t}||² from H_{t→t+1}H_{t+1→t}=I, applied on the reversed pair as a self-supervised signal, added to the regression loss (all weights 1.0).
Dropout pseudo-ensemble: Dropout (p=0.2) on the last two FC layers, with test-time weight scaling instead of multiple forward passes, to mimic an ensemble in a single pass.
Depth discretization: one-hot encoding of depth into N (10) equidistant bins over 0-10 m, so small depth noise does not change the representation.

Soft egocentric top-down projection: back-project depth to a 3D point cloud, orthographically project to (x,z), count points per cell and normalize to [0,1]; this makes subtle depth noise more robust.
Action-specific models (SepAct): separate VO networks for move-forward, turn-left and turn-right, because their SE(2) distributions differ and the data is imbalanced.

Integration with policy: VO trained offline on 1M frame pairs from 24,286 shortest-path trajectories in 72 Gibson-4+ scenes, then plugged into a pretrained DD-PPO policy, optionally fine-tuning the policy for 14.7M frames.

setting.backbone: ResNet-18 VO model (trained from scratch, supervised + self-supervised) plus a pretrained DD-PPO ResNet-18 + 2-layer LSTM policy
setting.model_size: VO ~3.93M params per action (3×3.96M for SepAct)
setting.training_data: VO: 1M pairs from 72 Gibson-4+ training scenes with noise models; policy: DD-PPO pretrained with GPS+Compass, optionally fine-tuned for 14.7M frames with VO
setting.observation: egocentric noisy RGB-D (341x192, 70° FoV), no GPS+Compass
setting.action_space: discrete: move forward 0.25m, turn left/right 30°, stop (noisy actuation, no sliding)
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT SE(2) used only to train VO)

numbers_note: Benchmark is Habitat Challenge 2020 PointNav (Gibson), mapped to Gibson-PointNav; the 'val' rows are the offline Gibson-4+ validation split.
results: Full VO integration reaches 71.7% SR / 52.5% SPL on the Habitat Challenge 2020 test-standard, beating the prior best (Karkus et al., 64.5% SR / 37.7% SPL) while running 6.4x faster (5.83 vs 37.5 h). On validation, VO without fine-tuning gets 81% SR against 97% with perfect GPS+Compass.
limitations: Still a gap to perfect localization (81-82% vs 97% SR on val), and VO drift accumulates over long trajectories.
Requires separate models per action and known camera intrinsics, and assumes planar SE(2) motion on a single floor.
Evaluated only in simulation with modeled noise; no real-robot experiments.
compares_to: Ramakrishnan et al. (occupancy anticipation + Active Neural SLAM)
